summary:
Radar for 2026-11-19 (GLP-1 focus). Most of the opportunity is in one story: Foundayo (orforglipron), an approved pill people already search for by name. It was registered in Australia on Nov 16 (the TGA, Australia's medicines regulator) and approved by Health Canada on Nov 18. Both countries have high ad rates. This fits our fast-turn rule, and our Foundayo video is already gaining about 30 minutes a day, so the queued "Foundayo: What to Expect" long video should move to the front with a CA/AU hook.

The second strongest is the FDA's class-wide NAION eye warning. I confirmed it was announced on Nov 9; The Hill, News-Medical and Medical Daily (the Denmark compensation story) all covered it again on Nov 19. It's peaking, but it's a label change and a search-demand format.

Next: a Thanksgiving peak (The Conversation and Newswise guides both ran today), Health Canada's new Mounjaro heart indication (the SURPASS-CVOT head-to-head against dulaglutide, Nov 18), and the Washington Post's Nov 18 piece on lifting weights. The evergreen searched formats (hair loss, nausea, injection sites, months 2–6, head-to-head against semaglutide, serious risks) are refreshed by this week's news.

Lower down are three stories that need care. The "why GLP-1s don't work for everyone" ScienceDaily piece turned out to be a Conversation essay about a semaglutide study still under way, not a result. The UK nutrient-shortfall study is small and observational. The semaglutide binge-eating trial touches eating disorders.

Rejected: psychosis case reports after abruptly stopping GLP-1s, employer coverage, "GLP-1 vacations", compounded or telehealth warning letters, stock and licensing deals, and microdosing.

candidates.topic: Foundayo (orforglipron) now approved in Canada (Health Canada, Nov 18) and Australia (TGA, Nov 16): what to expect from the approved label
candidates.angle: Long form, 'Orforglipron (Foundayo) Pill: What to Expect'. Re-render the queued 11-11 script with a sentence-1 hook: 'If your doctor in Canada or Australia just mentioned the new GLP-1 pill…'. Cover who it's approved for, how the daily pill differs from a weekly pen (no food or water timing rules, per the label), common GI effects and when they usually ease, the label's top dose 17.2 mg with −11.1% (trial figures labelled as trial). No dose steps. Watch-next link to How It Works. Short: 'Foundayo is a pill, so why does it still cause nausea?'
candidates.predicted_peak: 3–10 days (Australian pharmacy launch plus Canadian coverage)
candidates.why_now: Two new approvals in high-ad-rate markets within 72 hours. AU GP outlets (RACGP, AusDoc, Medical Republic) and CityNews say it can be prescribed now and is reaching shelves within days. Our existing Foundayo video already gains about 30 minutes a day from 'foundayo' searches. This is the EloraTZP fast-turn model on an approved drug.

evidence.signal: TGA registered Foundayo on 16 Nov 2026 for adults with obesity, or overweight with a weight-related condition, and for type 2 diabetes. Available within days.
Health Canada approves Eli Lilly's GLP-1 pill for weight loss (18 Nov)
Canadian Foundayo product page (use for Canada-specific label wording)
US approval on 1 Apr 2026, the fastest approval of a new molecular entity since 2002 (US label baseline)

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro/Zepbound) eye warning: what the FDA's class-wide NAION label change says, how rare it is, and which sudden vision changes need care right away
candidates.angle: Calm, label-first explainer: 'Tirzepatide's new eye warning: how rare is it?' The FDA's figure is about 6.4 vs 3.8 events per 100,000 people per year, from 126 trials and over 134,000 patients (verify on the FDA page before scripting). Sudden, painless vision loss in one eye means urgent care. Any medication questions go to the prescriber, with no stopping advice. Name both NANOS and the AAO if cited. This can also be a chapter in Serious Risks.
candidates.why_now: The FDA announced the class-wide label change on Nov 9. Coverage is still landing on Nov 19 (The Hill's 'eye stroke' piece, News-Medical, Medical Daily on Denmark paying 31 users). Our NAION TikTok reached 471 views. Label-change videos are a proven search-demand format.

evidence.signal: FDA requires class-wide GLP-1 RA labeling changes for potential NAION risk (Nov 9, 2026)
Warning applies across the class, including tirzepatide and orforglipron
'The GLP-1 blind spot: why the FDA's new eye stroke warning matters' (Nov 19)
Consumer explainer of the FDA requirement and the incidence figures

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) and your heart: SURPASS-CVOT head-to-head vs dulaglutide (Trulicity), now with a Health Canada heart-risk indication (Nov 18)
candidates.angle: 'Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) and Your Heart: What the Trial Showed.' Give the result and the population (adults with type 2 diabetes and established cardiovascular disease) in one sentence, with the comparator on screen. Explain what an approved heart-risk indication means for questions to bring to your doctor. Keep it separate from SELECT (semaglutide, no diabetes). Watch-next link to Side Effects.

The 'you' scenario goes in sentence 1, then a second payoff by 30 s (when GI effects typically ease, per the label). Average weight trajectory from SURMOUNT-1 in its full population. candidates.topic: Tirzepatide vs semaglutide head-to-head: what SURMOUNT-5 showed (Zepbound vs Wegovy)
candidates.angle: Approved-drug head-to-head against tirzepatide. 'Tirzepatide vs Semaglutide: Which Lost More in the Trial?' The question stays in the title. Result plus population (adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition, without diabetes; open-label, 72 weeks) in one sentence. The fact-checker confirms the figures from the NEJM paper. Close on what side effects looked like in both arms and 'talk to your prescriber'. No switching advice.
keywords: which is better zepbound or wegovy
candidates.predicted_peak: evergreen; extra lift from coverage questions
candidates.why_now: Drug-versus-drug searches are a 10–195x format in this niche. This week's employer-coverage stories (NBC) push people to compare options, which is our search hook; cost itself stays out. Tirzepatide-vs-semaglutide observational papers (rotator cuff, CKM stage 2) are rising on PubMed but are context only.

candidates.angle: A broad Lane A question that also suits the Plateau retitle ('Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) Stopped Working? What Trials Show'). Use SURMOUNT-1's spread of results in the full population. The Alberta metabolic-adaptation work is a semaglutide study still under way: say 'researchers are testing' and claim no result. Rare GLP1R variants (Nature Metabolism) count as early research only. No weight-loss-pressure framing; include support resources. The Editor-in-Chief must review it.
